comments.body:
## 1. Charter, method, evidence base (2026-09-06)

Operator ask: this project has seen a progressive increase in complexity. Present proposals to simplify, one at a time, in plain language with tradeoffs; assess each against the ADRs and ticket history; compare architectural changes to popular OSS practice; after reviewing all proposals together, create an epic of the approved work. Later refined: right-size the work into several epics that can run in parallel with reduced file-impact overlap; stories free of uncertainty (no "or", "spike", "TBD"); research or experiment now to de-risk; include other deprecated functionality, aliases and config keys because the release is a single breaking release.

Method: six read-only subagent shards audited the repository (reconciler/bridge; LLM review gates; workflow engine, editor, evals, overlap, grounding; store/CLI/config surfaces; trust/MCP/review-bot/metrics/infra/CI/scripts; tests/docs/ADRs/ticket history). Each finding was cross-referenced to ADRs and ticket history, then synthesized into 21 proposals. Basis: local checkout e510c64; origin/main moved from 32d0df6 through 2e81cb9767c1, 083620b0, 4c77d6f3e96f to 360d504f5ceb during the session.

Evidence base: src grew 1.3 MB to 8.8 MB of Python (124 to 671 files) between 2026-06-15 and 09-06; tests 2.1 to 18 MB (246 to 1,846 files); ADRs 0 to 116; docs 16 to 238. Bugs created per fortnight from May 31: 39, 32, 107, 107, 275, 237, 331. Close classes of closed bugs: preexisting 35 percent, plan_defect 15 percent, regression 10 percent. Bug-title clusters: gates and attestation about 240, store/git/lock about 190, reconciler about 175, CI/deploy about 110, MCP about 70.

The 21 proposals (A remove / B consolidate / C tests, docs, ADRs):
A. P1 overlap/enrichment (ADR 0086): ~2.6k src, 4-9k tests, 14 env vars, 71.5 percent of store event files, 0 findings in 2,093 reviews, ~31 percent of LLM calls. P2 Jira Data Center + pandoc wiki + DC harness (ADR 0055/0095/0096). P3 BPMN editor + Node tier (ADR 0071 never implemented): ~5.7k src, 2.1 MB tracked dist, 205 MB node_modules. P4 remote op-cert service + API Gateway + 4 unused MCP auth modes. P5 freeze identity/authorship signing. P6 S3 backend (ADR 0093). P7 never-firing plan criteria, inert Pass-3 floors, never-blocking code-review overlays. P8 cutover leftovers (reconciler summary-executor trio, CREATE_ROUTE/WRITE_FACADE legacy, reconcile-check residue, payload shadow, --filter-local-ids; LLM discovery_shadow, parity.py, review_workflows, _review_ticket_impl, shim.py, HMAC verify). P9 evals/calibration/experiments out of the wheel, consumed one-shots, advisory CI, grounding tiers. P10 metrics to scripts, audit web UI, tracing, one-shot scripts, retired infra scripts.
B. P11 74 CLI verbs to ~36 via noun groups. P12 one typed operation registry generating argparse + FastMCP + outputSchema from annotated library functions. P13 reconciler as a normal package, in-process. P14 one retry helper, one lock module, collapse completion recovery. P15 stop producing compaction snapshots. P16 config/env: empty alias machinery, 13 warn tombstones, rollback toggles' legacy branches, test hooks in production, one precedence implementation, env registry derivation. P17 attestation staleness 16 verdicts to 4. P18 snapshot cache: drop ticket-pinned view, hardlink deltas, detached GC worker. P19 bridge residue: bridge_state/ never pruned, [mapping] overlay, two-witness bug auto-filing, sidecars.
C. P20 tests: merge 88 held-out twins (17.8k LOC), delete 37 seam/split guards (7k), collapse 3 CI-parity guards, one owner per check_* gate. P21 docs/ADRs: docs/experiments (13 MB) to evals/, evidence records to tickets, two stub docs, stale ADR headers, reconciler ADR consolidation.

The full proposal document with per-item tradeoffs and OSS comparisons lived in the session scratch directory (complexity-proposals-2026-09-06.md); its headline content is recorded here and its decisions in entry 2.

## 2. Operator rulings on the 21 proposals and the deprecation census

Section A rulings (2026-09-06). P1: a real gap (similar tickets are not surfaced at create); disabled for performance as implemented; preserve the design; deep dive requested and delivered (entry 3); P1-A approved: design-record epic plus removal referencing the removal commit; T1 lexical search judged insufficient against the historical corpus; the next iteration is vector search over ticket summaries, research out of scope for this session. P2, P4, P6: REJECTED as a class, with the operator's correction recorded verbatim in spirit: rebar is a tool used by clients; the fact that this project does not use Jira DC, the S3 backend, the MCP auth modes or the remote op-cert service itself is not a justification to retire client-facing functionality. P3: APPROVED; record the removal commit on the related idea epic yip-gem-teak so the editor can be restored. P5: REJECTED; identity is a core feature and the verify-identity job skips when enforcement is off (the audit misread it). P7: REJECTED. P8: APPROVED as the exemplar of the target class (finished cutovers with retained rollback twins). P9: the hard-coded repository paths in plan-replay, fixture-mining and provider-parity are a bug; those harnesses must be exposed to client projects that supply their own criteria; the remainder of P9 was withdrawn as an unclear assortment. P10: REJECTED; metrics and the audit web UI are kept features.

Section B and C rulings (2026-09-06 round 3). P11 APPROVED: hard cutover, no working aliases, every doc surface accurate, release notes list each rename; the existing removed-name hint mechanism is kept and populated as the forward-compatibility mechanism for future releases. P12: full generation REJECTED; a narrow MCP-only staged version APPROVED (annotate library params, advertise canonical JSON schemas, derive the 48 library-backed tools) with an ADR superseding topaz-blubbery-mice's no-generated-adapters clause for MCP only, justified by the post-oracle escape lowly-lawrencium-ovenbird. P13 APPROVED with revisions: real package, delete by-path loaders, extract a guarded pass core (bug: the library/MCP path runs an unlocked live pass), collapse only the middle subprocess hop; the subprocess boundary itself stays because no ADR ever chose it and reversing it needs one. P14 WITHDRAWN by me: the combination was previously rejected (epic civil-marlin-flare, ADR 0103, ADR 0107, ADR 0031), the counts were inflated by category errors, and I had conflated the store write lock with the reconciler pass lock; survivors folded into P8. P15 and P18: flagged by the premise re-check as deployment-specific evidence and not carried into this pass. P16 APPROVED including removal of tombstoned entries as a one-time documented break; the unknown-config-key warning is kept and extended to the reserved [llm] table as the forward-compatibility mechanism. P17 REJECTED as an oversimplification; its residue APPROVED only after independent confirmation the code is dead (done, entry 3). P19 APPROVED after verification (no retention; keep-last-N). P20 and P21 APPROVED. HMAC retirement APPROVED after verification that the live tracker holds only op-cert signatures.

Deprecation census outcomes (origin/main 8ae0d11b at census time): the alias registry is already empty; 20 tombstones all mislabeled removed_in=v1.0.0; 13 warn-class tombstones removed, the 6 error-class rows kept with their real removed_in versions (v0.8.0 for five, v0.12.0 for REBAR_LLM_MODEL); REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE=github-api retired; internal re-export shims removed per ADR 0111; review_workflows.py, uvicorn_graceful_seconds alias, MCP_ENV_VARS deprecated flags, severity dead code, shadow comparators, STATUS_GATING comments, doc drift and CHANGELOG bookkeeping folded into the epics. Kept: about 600 persisted-data read-compatibility sites (store format gate, alias backfill, SCHEMA_VERSION folds, binding legacy merge, sidecar readers, workflow DSL shims, ensure units). Operator decisions on the census: warn tombstones go, error rows stay with real versions; the unknown-key default is not flipped; bare 4-hex ticket ids stay silently accepted and undocumented (an intentional undocumented feature so agents do not adopt them); the single-pass review engine is a demo to retire completely, not just its harness; the four-phase plan review and four-phase code review are the real reviews.

## 3. Research records

P1 deep dive (three subagents). Implementation: overlap never ran at CREATE, only after plan-review certification; digests and queue coordination were persisted as events on the shared auto-pushed tickets branch; no persisted index, so each query re-reduced every ticket (about 48 s on this store); 105,197 of 147,074 event files (71.5 percent) were overlap sidecars; 93 percent of digests were recomputed for unchanged content; the drain gate rode every store write and spawned a detached interpreter. Reusable: the ticket_digest schema and prompt, the BM25F scorer, graph exclusion, the judge prompt and batch contract, the calibration data, the content-hash freshness idea, and recent_creates.py as the model for per-clone derived state. Ticket history: epic only-crave-art (bd83-c56f-1f72-4ef2), seven children landed 07-09/10, ADR 0086; embeddings were rejected on an eight-pair experiment; six bug clusters all trace to the architecture (prune outside the lock, prune breaking union-merge, unbounded growth and write storms, an O(store) gate on every write, an unbounded judge, detached-child hygiene); create-time was never wired; 44 of 51 real duplicate pairs are semantic not lexical; the 08-31 disable also disabled the same-title journal. OSS survey (git-bug, Fossil, jj, Cargo, Zoekt, Gitea, Zulip, Discourse, Bugzilla, GitLab, GitHub, Linear, Sentry): every comparable system keeps the index as a disposable, version-keyed local cache outside the replicated store, caught up in the reader's process, with compose-time similarity lexical-first and non-blocking and any model call off the write path. Synthesis: right retrieval pattern, wrong persistence and coordination architecture (ADR 0086 section 3, the event store as queue and cache). Recommended next shape: per-clone SQLite index keyed by tickets HEAD SHA and format version, catch-up in the reader, create-time query top 3 to 5 advisory, LLM judge on demand; the operator's framing is vector search over summaries (Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 identified as the candidate model). Recorded as the design-record epic fattish-plucky-bufflehead and its research story.

P12 versus the janitor's RP08 rejection. RP08 rested on topaz-blubbery-mice (no generated adapters, Pattern A) and ruinable-cozey-caracal. The revisit bar was a post-oracle escape and it was met once: lowly-lawrencium-ovenbird (2026-09-02) found the MCP output mirror under-declared 41 schema properties. ADR 0100 section 2's non-derivable CLI cases stand. Verdict: reject P12 in full, stage P12 narrow for MCP only. Experiments later confirmed the FastMCP mechanism (a dict return gets a pass-through RootModel; setting fn_metadata.output_schema to an inlined canonical schema is advertised and validated; inlining is mandatory because jsonschema cannot resolve cross-file refs), measured the null-versus-absent wire delta (show_ticket 44 keys and 12 nulls on the wire versus 36 and 6 from the library) and enumerated eight input divergences for the override table.

P13. The bridge runs _bridge_runner -> rebar bridge sync -> python -m rebar_reconciler; _lib_ops._bridge_run bypasses the guarded core so MCP bridge_sync runs an unlocked live pass; the outer 3600 s kill orphans the grandchild. Fix: one guarded core, direct spawn with start_new_session and process-group reaping, subprocess boundary kept.

P17 residue confirmed dead on origin/main via Serena plus git grep: the _hash_basis(at_current_gate_ref=) branch, read_set.terraform_membership_entries, identical CLOSE and DRIFT_REFRESH profiles, a duplicated unresolvable-ref message, and the not-closed verdict unreachable from plan_review_status. _legacy_material_ok is live and kept.

P19 verified: repo-root bridge_state/ snapshots, sync logs, alerts and the sync-route manifest have no retention; the snapshot is a same-pass round trip; a client at 1,000 issues hourly writes about 0.8 GB per day. Fix: keep-last-5 snapshots and sync logs, 30 alert days, prune in persist_and_log, move to .rebar/bridge/.

HMAC. All 3,883 live SIGNATURE events on this tracker are Ed25519 op-certs; story 8f1d's contract phase already refuses the legacy scheme for both op-cert kinds; the HMAC module only verifies records nothing mints. Retiring it means non-envelope records read as unsigned with a retired-scheme reason; worst case is a re-review, never store breakage.

## 5. Baseline maintenance: the decision, its history, and the bug it exposed

The two ratchets keep committed lists: .github/complexity-baseline.json (per-function McCabe ceilings, shrink-only) and .github/mechanism-baseline.json (censused mechanisms by kind and name). Removing something leaves a stale row. For the complexity list, stale rows are tolerated by make lint and CI since bug dystopian-bardlike-basil (d319-a094-4ee7-4549) fixed the contradiction in August. For the mechanism list they are not: tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py::test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree asserts set(baseline) | admitted == live, so a change that deletes a censused mechanism must also drop its row, and the only tool that drops rows is --update-stale (precedent: commit 81da792, which retired the HLC switch). AGENTS.md calls that flag maintenance-only.

History of why hand edits are prohibited: task 47e9 (janitor 2026-08-06) locked the complexity baseline with a CI step (--lock) that diffs the change against main's merge base and rejects any added key, administrator force-submit being the designed override; a path re-spell is a remove plus an add and cannot be told from a smuggled ceiling. The mechanism baseline has no CI lock; the prohibition is the operator's 2026-09-06 ruling on celadon-computable-smelts (a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a): mechanisms must not require exception routes, agents abuse exception paths, the baseline must not become contributor-editable; the sanctioned paths are "land it, change nothing" for reductions and the mechanism-ok marker for additions. Change 2658's agent hand-added two rows to get past the tests and that was recorded as a guidance violation.

Defect found: _run_update_stale (scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py:177-195) refuses on compare()'s marker-blind has_regression (scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:45-57), while the gate's evaluate() and the unit tests honour markers. Consequence, proven live on origin/main 4c77d6f3e96f in a scratch worktree: seven marker-admitted mechanisms already exist without baseline rows (autouse_fixture::tests/conftest.py::_one_engine_root and six ci_gate entries), so --update-stale refuses on an unmodified checkout, which blocks every one of the ten breaking-pass stories that delete a mechanism. The one-function fix (replace the compare/has_regression refusal with evaluate(current, baseline, markers_for(repo_root)) and refuse on a nonzero code) was applied in the scratch worktree: --check and --update-stale exit 0 with the baseline byte-identical, and a scratch regression test failed on the unfixed script at assert rc == 0 and passed with the fix (35 passed with the existing 33). Filed as bug amoeboid-amateur-guillemot (1768-5b6f-958a-43e9, priority 1, discovered_from a1f1) with the diff and evidence in its first comment; the overlap, editor, reconciler, LLM-leftovers, HMAC, MCP and config epics depend on it.

Operator decisions (approved 2026-09-07): (1) the same-change drain stays the rule for removals; AGENTS.md and docs/architecture.md are reworded and --update-stale made marker-aware by the bug fix; (2) the reconciler package-move story keeps its six-key complexity-baseline re-spell and the operator force-submits that one change once the lock step is its only red CI item, the implementing agent handing off and never overriding; (3) the 29-key mechanism-baseline re-spell in the test-package rename is a sanctioned one-time maintenance edit named in the commit message, with a reviewer check posted on the story (strip the moved prefix, sort name and value, diff main against the change, expect no difference). Additional finding from the experiments: the complexity map must be re-sorted, not just substituted, because reconciler/ sorts after the underscore-prefixed keys and an unsorted file fails --check.

comments.body:
## 9. Analysis: what would have caught the complexity, and the janitor

Recorded in full as idea doomed-soldierly-slothbear (77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec); summary here.

Gate timeline: plan-review claim gate and criteria registry 2026-06-23; LLM-Review label 06-29; module-size cap 07-18; complexity ratchet 08-05; mechanism ratchet 09-01 (Track I stability epic wide-wimpy-insect, not the janitor). The only complexity-aimed plan criterion, A1 (over-engineering, NIH, config-surface proliferation), is advisory; G6 approach soundness, E4 premise and G1G2 edit-set are blocking and work well at grounding (all four land-first stories blocked in round 1 on grounding defects, correctly). The code gate blocks only security; deletion-impact, scope-intent and tests are advisory. The mechanism ratchet blocks adding a mechanism and never checks a retired one was removed. The completion verifier checks the acceptance criteria as written. No gate asks whether the system is simpler afterward.

Five classes of removed complexity and the missing check for each: (1) cutover residue with no "old path deleted" criterion: sunset ticket named on every toggle or mechanism-ok marker, verified deterministically at that ticket's close, T12 rollout overlay blocking for toggles; (2) copies policed instead of collapsed (MCP drift gate 08-07, parity manifest 09-01): promote A1's NIH facet to blocking when a plan adds a ci_gate kind; (3) gate-induced tests (four seam-guard files written by module-size-cap split commits 07-30, 08-13, 08-19; 88 held-out twins from the rebar-implement convention; 30 modules re-running lint scripts): a test taxonomy in the code-review tests overlay, a held-out merge phase in rebar-implement, behaviour-test criteria for split stories; (4) speculative features (editor bundle under a Proposed ADR, overlap switched off within three weeks): deterministic no-shipped-artifact-for-Proposed-ADR check, decision ticket for config-disabled features past a window; (5) pre-gate structure (by-path package loading, 06-08), paid once. Highest-leverage single change: a blocking net-mechanism criterion (a plan adding a ratchet-counted mechanism names the one it retires or carries an A1 justification; the ratchet docstring records 56 percent of sampled fixes add a mechanism).

Janitor: premise sound, objective and output contract wrong. Its floor (validity 0.75, impact 0.5, reachable harm) selects defects, whose remediation adds mechanism; "never edits code" turns tidying into 20 to 37 tickets per run with no net budget; plans are approved against a frozen snapshot while main moves. Evidence that janitor remediation produced what this pass deletes: RP-04's WRITE_FACADE switch, the eight seam_clean_heldout tests and the config-ownership gate; RP-03's _call_with_retry and CREATE_ROUTE toggle; the 08-06 run's MCP drift gate and complexity CI lock; the 08-29 run's alias tombstones (landed 09-04, deleted three days later), its rejection of shared MCP contracts followed by the parity manifest (09-01, deleted six days later), and its scanner-integration child whose wholesale revert removed the mechanism-ok test contract and is the ancestor of bug 1768; the comment-condensation sweep of about 1,700 per-file tasks whose commits invalidated cites in six of our stories and whose worktrees held the host's gate slots. Not the janitor: the duplicate-ticket incident (tier-2 replay harness) and the mechanism ratchet. Proposed: split into a deletion-only tidying janitor judged by net LOC and non-positive mechanism delta with a per-run ticket cap and a week-later measurement, and a separate less frequent defect audit; the janitor files no gates; discovery against a SHA with 24-hour approval; no per-file mechanical sweeps; held-out merging and seam-guard deletion move into rebar-implement's epic close.

## 10. Process notes, lessons, open items

Interruptions and recoveries: a session rate limit on 2026-09-06 killed five spec agents mid-run; specs were persisted and relaunched without subagents. On 2026-09-07 the rebar MCP server was slow enough that reads moved to the background and a summary call timed out at 300 s; then the MCP OAuth token expired for this session and for a running subagent, which had verified six cite corrections but could not write them. The operator confirmed the local CLI is the authorized path in that state, and the corrections were applied through it; plan review round 5 also runs through the CLI, unbounded and in the background, per the AGENTS.md rule against timing out gate operations.

Agent-quality lessons recorded: (a) reviewers were right every round, and each block was a grounding defect I could have caught with one more grep; the recurring miss was multi-line parenthesized imports invisible to single-line patterns; (b) an acceptance check that cannot fail (\s in git grep) is worse than none; (c) my "three-round rule" was an invented constraint, corrected; (d) the first cite-fix agent died on a rate limit with nothing written, the second on the token expiry; staging work as files before writing let it survive both; (e) two agent reports needed correction for internal count inconsistencies before ticketing (E10 CI-parity counts; E3 loader cites), and one agent's initial verdict on the duplicate-ticket incident wrongly blamed the janitor sweeps before experiment corrected it to the tier-2 harness.

Durable locations: every epic's first comment holds its research record; every story's first comment holds its mechanics; this log and idea 77e3 hold the analysis; session scratch (proposal document, agent reports, overlap and drift analyses, cite-fix staging) is under the job's temporary directory and is not durable, so nothing decision-bearing was left only there.
